column1: # What `seetrex-verifier verify-anchor --kit <v2 kit> --monitor <bundle>` REALLY
# prints on stdout for a confirmed run with no anomalous rotation, in this tree:
# the WHOLE block from the banner to the COMPLETITUD line, every line, in order.
# The binary then prints one empty line and the scope footer
# (`seetrex_verifier::scope::SCOPE_ANCHOR`), and nothing after it.
# This file is an OBSERVATION, not a claim. `crates/verifier/tests/intent_record.rs`
# (`test_intent_anchor_capture_lines_are_measured_not_parsed`) spawns the built
# executable on a synthetic v2 kit and monitor bundle, fills every placeholder
# with the value that run must print, and asserts that the process's stdout is
# EXACTLY these rows, in this order, followed by the empty line and the footer.
# No line of the block can be reworded, added, dropped or moved in the binary
# without this file moving with it.
# A private consumer (the kit's documentation test) reads this file instead of
# parsing the verifier's source: it fills each placeholder with the value the
# capture in section 7.1 of the auditor kit shows and compares the result with
# the captured block, whole lines, in order.
# Format: <key><TAB><line>, one row per printed line, in the order printed.
# <key> names the row and is never printed. <line> is byte for byte what the
# binary prints, leading spaces included, except for PLACEHOLDERS: `{name}`,
# with `name` in lowercase letters and `_`, stands for ONE value that depends
# on the run (a count, the tenant) and nothing else; the text around it is
# fixed. No other `{` or `}` appears in a line. Each consumer must fill every
# placeholder it finds and must use every value it brings: an unknown name or
# an unused value is a failure, never a skip.
# Placeholders: {tenant} the kit's tenant_slug; {anchored} anchored leaves of
# the package; {rotations} rotations of the package; {keys} identity keys
# derived; {signatures} submitter signatures checked; {discarded} monitor
# leaves discarded; {rows} rows of the package the truncation rule judged
# against (no --chain).
banner
tenant
anchored leaves
rotations
identity keys
submitter signatures
column2: submitter signatures:    {signatures} checked against the keys of the kit

column1: monitor leaves
column2: monitor leaves:          {discarded} discarded (in the log under a key of the kit, without its signature: not counted for COMPLETITUD)

column1: truncation reference
column2: truncation reference:    package rows only, {rows} rows (no --chain; heads past N are UNDECIDABLE)

column1: completitud
column2: COMPLETITUD:             CONFIRMED OFFLINE (monitor supplied; enumeration completeness = trusted input)
